test_title: PYST 13: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - GA (Held On 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 14**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 14** of the **Constitution of India** provides that the **State** shall not deny to any person **equality before the law** or the **equal protection of the laws** within the territory of **India**. *Hence, this option is correct.*
 
• The term **"Equality before the law"** is of **British origin** and implies the absence of any special privileges in favor of any individual. It signifies the equal subjection of all persons to the ordinary law of the land.
 
• The term **"Equal protection of the laws"** is derived from **Section 1** of the **14th Amendment** of the **U.S. Constitution**. It implies that among equals, the law should be equal and equally administered, and that like should be treated alike.
 
• This right is available to all **persons**, whether **citizens** or **foreigners**. It also extends to **legal persons**, such as **statutory corporations**, **companies**, **registered societies**, or any other type of legal entity.
 
• The **Supreme Court** has held that **Article 14** is a **"Basic Structure"** of the **Constitution**. Therefore, it cannot be destroyed even by an amendment to the Constitution under **Article 368**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 19:**
 
 
• It guarantees to all citizens the **six rights** regarding freedom of: (a) **speech and expression**, (b) **assembly**, (c) **association**, (d) **movement**, (e) **residence**, and (f) **profession**.
 
• These rights are available only to **citizens** and not to foreigners or legal entities like companies. *Hence, Article 19 is not the correct answer.*
 
 
 
• **Article 21:**
 
 
• It declares that no person shall be deprived of his **life or personal liberty** except according to **procedure established by law**.
 
• This right is available to both **citizens and non-citizens**. Over the years, the judiciary has expanded its scope to include the **right to privacy**, **right to health**, and **right to free legal aid**. *Hence, Article 21 is not the correct answer.*
 
 
 
• **Article 32:**
 
 
• It provides the **Right to Constitutional Remedies**, allowing citizens to move the **Supreme Court** for the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights**.
 
• **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** described this article as the **"Heart and Soul of the Constitution"**. Under this, the court can issue **writs** like **Habeas Corpus**, **Mandamus**, and **Certiorari**. *Hence, Article 32 is not the correct answer.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The concept of **Rule of Law** is the basis of **Article 14**. It was famously propounded by the British jurist **A.V. Dicey**. His theory has three elements: absence of arbitrary power, equality before the law, and the primacy of the rights of the individual.
 
• There are certain **exceptions** to the rule of equality. For instance, the **President of India** and the **Governors of States** enjoy immunities under **Article 361**. They are not answerable to any court for the exercise and performance of the powers and duties of their office.
 
• **Article 31-C** is also an exception; the **Supreme Court** held that "where **Article 31-C** comes in, **Article 14** goes out." This relates to laws giving effect to certain **Directive Principles** (Article 39(b) and 39(c)).
 
• Foreign sovereigns (ambassadors and diplomats) enjoy immunity from **civil and criminal proceedings** in **India**, as per international conventions.
